name: Measles & vaccine-preventable
value: US 4,852 cases in 2026 (29 Oct); infant deaths
summary: Infant measles deaths in New York and Wisconsin; US at 4,852 cases; elimination review due in November
state: An infant in Lewis County, New York, died on 2 Nov, and the CDC had confirmed 4,852 US cases in 2026 as of 29 Oct, against 2,289 in all of 2025; regional health authorities are due to review US elimination status in November (EMJ). Wisconsin announced its first measles death in 36 years, an infant, on 5 Nov, with 431 cases in the state (MPR News). ECDC's 6 Nov update shows 66 cases across 13 European countries in September, so a multi-country surge with rising deaths is not established.
for_you: Unvaccinated people and infants too young for vaccination are most at risk. The NHS and UKHSA publish MMR vaccination guidance; US readers can check CDC and state health department advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: large outbreaks in a high-income country (US 4,852 cases to 29 Oct); multi-country surge with rising deaths not confirmed

sources.title: EMJ — New York measles death amid US outbreak

why: Falling vaccination rates are bringing back diseases once eliminated; measles is the canary for the rest.

rubric.alert: Multi-country surge with rising deaths, or polio/diphtheria resurgence in high-income countries.
rubric.watch: Large outbreaks in high-income countries, or loss of elimination status.
rubric.normal: No large outbreaks in high-income countries.
